mcqs.question: In a convex lens, where is the principal focus located?

options.A: At the optical centre of the lens
options.B: On the principal axis, at a distance equal to the focal length from the optical centre on the side opposite the object
options.D: At the position of the object

mcqs.answer: On the principal axis, at a distance equal to the focal length from the optical centre on the side opposite the object
mcqs.explanation: The principal focus of a convex lens lies on the principal axis at a distance equal to the focal length (f) from the optical centre, on the side opposite to the incoming light. It is not at the centre, at infinity, or at the object position.

mcqs.question: The focal length of a thin lens is defined as:

options.A: The distance between the two principal foci
options.B: The distance between the optical centre and the principal focus
options.C: The radius of curvature of the lens surface
options.D: The distance from the lens to the object when the image is formed at infinity

mcqs.answer: The distance between the optical centre and the principal focus
mcqs.explanation: Focal length (f) is the distance from the optical centre (O) of a thin lens to its principal focus (F). Option A describes the distance between two foci, which is 2f for a convex lens. Option C is unrelated, and D describes object distance for an object at infinity, not the definition of f.

mcqs.question: Which of the following rays is NOT used in the standard ray diagram for a convex lens?

options.A: A ray passing through the optical centre of the lens
options.B: A ray parallel to the principal axis that passes through the principal focus after refraction
options.C: A ray passing through the principal focus before reaching the lens and emerging parallel to the principal axis
options.D: A ray that reflects off the lens surface and follows the law of reflection

mcqs.answer: A ray that reflects off the lens surface and follows the law of reflection
mcqs.explanation: Standard ray diagrams for lenses use three rays: (i) through the optical centre, (ii) parallel then through focus, and (iii) through focus then parallel. Reflection does not occur in refraction through lenses, so option D is not used.

mcqs.question: An object is placed at a distance of 2f from a convex lens of focal length f. What is the nature and position of the image formed?

options.A: Real, inverted, same size as the object, formed at 2f on the opposite side
options.B: Real, inverted, reduced, formed between f and 2f on the opposite side
options.C: Virtual, upright, enlarged, formed beyond 2f on the same side as the object
options.D: Virtual, upright, same size as the object, formed at the focal point

mcqs.answer: Real, inverted, reduced, formed between f and 2f on the opposite side
mcqs.explanation: For a convex lens, when the object is placed beyond 2f, the image is real, inverted, reduced, and lies between f and 2f on the opposite side of the lens. Option A would be correct only if the object were at 2f, giving same size; here the object is beyond 2f, so the image is reduced.

mcqs.question: Which type of lens will cause a set of parallel rays to diverge after passing through it?
mcqs.explanation: A concave (diverging) lens spreads parallel incident rays outward, making them appear to originate from a virtual focus on the same side as the object. A convex lens converges parallel rays to a real focus, so option A is incorrect. Options C and D are also incorrect.

mcqs.question: A thin lens is placed in the path of a narrow light ray, and the ray passes through the lens without any deviation. Which point of the lens does the ray most likely pass through?
mcqs.explanation: When a ray passes through the optical centre (the geometric centre) of a thin lens, it experiences negligible refraction and continues in the same direction. The principal focus, vertex, or edge would cause the ray to bend.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the principal focus of a lens is correct?

options.A: The principal focus coincides with the optical centre of the lens.
options.B: The principal focus is located at infinity for all lenses.
options.C: The principal focus lies on the principal axis at a distance equal to the focal length from the optical centre.
options.D: The principal focus is the point where the object must be placed to obtain a real image.

mcqs.answer: The principal focus lies on the principal axis at a distance equal to the focal length from the optical centre.
mcqs.explanation: The principal focus (F) is on the principal axis, at a distance f (the focal length) from the optical centre (O). It does not coincide with O (A), is not always at infinity (B), and the object position for a real image depends on object distance, not the focus (D).

mcqs.question: A convex lens forms an image of a distant (effectively at infinity) object at a point 10 cm behind the lens. What is the focal length of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: For an object at infinity, the image is formed at the focal point of a convex lens. Hence the distance of the image from the lens equals the focal length. Since the image is 10 cm behind the lens, the focal length is 10 cm.
